extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent applicants/attorneys
extracted.subtask_description: Examination and practitioner guidance on identifying, rejecting, and overcoming statutory and nonstatutory double patenting (including use of terminal disclaimers and joint research agreement/CREATE Act issues) in U.S. patent prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and requirements of a terminal disclaimer (37 CFR 1.321)
rubrics_metrics.description: A terminal disclaimer is a statement filed by an owner (in whole or in part) of a patent or a patent to be granted that is used to disclaim or dedicate a portion of the entire term of all the claims of a patent. The requirements for a terminal disclaimer are set forth in 37 CFR 1.321.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sample forms of a terminal disclaimer and guidance as to filing and treatment are provided in MPEP § 1490. See 37 CFR 1.321 for specific filing content and formal requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single terminal disclaimer for multiple commonly owned references
rubrics_metrics.description: To avoid paying multiple terminal disclaimer fees, a single terminal disclaimer based on common ownership may be filed in which the term disclaimed is based on all the conflicting, commonly owned double patenting references. Similarly, a single terminal disclaimer based on a joint research agreement may be filed in which the term disclaimed is based on all the conflicting double patenting references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each one of the commonly owned conflicting double patenting references must be included in the terminal disclaimer to avoid dual ownership problems if common ownership ceases. Include all conflicting references in the disclaimer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforceability provision required in terminal disclaimer (37 CFR 1.321(c)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: A terminal disclaimer for commonly owned conflicting claims must include a provision that any patent granted on that application shall be enforceable only for and during such period that said patent is commonly owned with the application or patent which formed the basis for the rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the disclaimer explicitly limits enforceability to the common ownership period to satisfy 37 CFR 1.321(c)(3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminal disclaimer requirements where invention resulted from joint research agreement (37 CFR 1.321(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.321(d) sets forth the requirements for a terminal disclaimer where the claimed invention resulted from activities undertaken within the scope of a joint research agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the claimed invention results from a joint research agreement, use the terminal disclaimer provisions at 37 CFR 1.321(d) and include the parties to the agreement as appropriate per statute and regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminal disclaimer required to overcome nonstatutory double patenting even after 35 U.S.C. 154(a)(2) change
rubrics_metrics.description: A terminal disclaimer under 37 CFR 1.321 is required in an application to overcome a nonstatutory double patenting rejection, even if the application was filed on or after June 8, 1995 and claims the benefit under 35 U.S.C. 120, 121, or 365(c) of the filing date of the patent or application which forms the basis for the rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite MPEP section or Official Gazette notice (1202 O.G. 112 (Sept. 30, 1997)) when applicants argue a terminal disclaimer should not be required due to 20-year term rules; terminal disclaimer still required because of patent term extension issues under 35 U.S.C. 154(b) and the enforceability-limiting provision in 37 CFR 1.321(c)(3).

rubrics_metrics.name: When double patenting rejection applies (commonly owned different inventive entities)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims in commonly owned applications of different inventive entities may be rejected on the ground of double patenting to prevent an organization from obtaining two or more patents with different expiration dates covering nearly identical subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use case law (e.g., In re Zickendraht; In re Christensen) to support that claims must be patentably distinct; mere form/content differences are insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double patenting for non-commonly owned inventions under joint research agreements (35 U.S.C. 103(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-commonly owned applications that claim inventions resulting from activities undertaken within the scope of a joint research agreement may be subject to double patenting treatment under the CREATE Act amendment to 35 U.S.C. 103(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply 35 U.S.C. 103(c) to permit treating certain non-commonly owned inventions as if commonly owned for obviousness/double-patenting purposes when statutory conditions are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedies to overcome double patenting rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: Double patenting rejections can be overcome by disclaiming, pursuant to 37 CFR 1.321(c), the terminal portion of the term of the later patent and including the enforceability provision, or in cases subject to a joint research agreement by disclaiming under 37 CFR 1.321(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Terminal disclaimer must contain required provisions and include all conflicting references when appropriate. Note: rejections under 35 U.S.C. 102 or 103 cannot be obviated solely by filing a terminal disclaimer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common ownership criteria (35 U.S.C. 103(c)(1) requirements)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications or patents are 'commonly owned' pursuant to 35 U.S.C. 103(c)(1) if they were wholly or entirely owned by the same person(s) or organization(s) at the time the claimed invention was made. Two inventions of different inventive entities come within the common ownership provisions when: (A) the later invention is not anticipated by the earlier invention under 35 U.S.C. 102; (B) the earlier invention qualifies as prior art for obviousness only under subsections (f) or (g) of 35 U.S.C. 102, or under 102(e) for certain dates; and (C) the inventions were, at the time the later invention was made, owned by the same person or subject to an obligation of assignment to the same person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 706.02(l)(2) for detailed common ownership definition and date-specific considerations for 102(e).

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint research agreement criteria (35 U.S.C. 103(c)(2) requirements)
rubrics_metrics.description: Two inventions come within the provisions of 35 U.S.C. 103(c)(2) when: (A) the later invention is not anticipated by the earlier invention under 35 U.S.C. 102; (B) the claimed invention was made by or on behalf of parties to a joint research agreement that was in effect on or before the date the claimed invention was made; (C) the claimed invention was made as a result of activities undertaken within the scope of the joint research agreement; and (D) the patent application discloses or is amended to disclose the names of the parties to the joint research agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A 'joint research agreement' is defined by 35 U.S.C. 103(c)(3) as a written contract, grant, or cooperative agreement entered into by two or more persons or entities for experimental, developmental, or research work in the field of the claimed invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner practice on timing of double patenting rejections and 102/103 rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner should make both a double patenting rejection based on common ownership and a rejection based on 35 U.S.C. 102(e)/103 prior art when the facts support both rejections. Until applicant has established that a reference is disqualified as prior art under the joint research agreement exclusion of 35 U.S.C. 103(c), the examiner should NOT apply a double patenting rejection based on a joint research agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 706.07(a) and § 804 for information when an Office action including a new subsequent double patenting rejection based on a reference disqualified under 103(c) may be made final.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of priority not required when 35 U.S.C. 103(c)(1) applies
rubrics_metrics.description: A determination of priority is not required when two inventions are commonly owned as set forth in 35 U.S.C. 103(c)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If 103(c) applies, the earlier invention is disqualified as prior art against the later invention and double patenting rejections can be used to ensure patents expire together; no prior-inventor determination needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.78(c) requirement to identify prior inventor when applicable
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 37 CFR 1.78(c), where an application or patent under reexamination and at least one other application naming different inventors are owned by the same person and contain conflicting claims, the Office may require the assignee to state whether the claimed inventions were commonly owned or, if not, indicate which named inventor is the prior inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraphs 8.27, 8.28 and 8.28.01 may be used to require the applicant to identify the prior inventor. Failure to comply with the requirement to name the prior inventor will result in abandonment of the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of form paragraph 8.27 (Different Inventors, Common Assignee, Same Invention)
rubrics_metrics.description: ¶ 8.27: Claim [1] directed to the same invention as that of claim [2] of commonly assigned [3]. The issue of priority under 35 U.S.C. 102(g) and possibly 35 U.S.C. 102(f) of this single invention must be resolved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when the claims listed are for the same invention (not merely obvious variants). The assignee is required to state which entity is the prior inventor. A terminal disclaimer has no effect in this situation since the basis is priority under 102(f)/(g). Insert appropriate data in brackets; see examiner notes for prerequisites and related form paragraphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of form paragraph 8.28 (Different Inventors, Common Assignee, Obvious Inventions, No Evidence of Common Ownership at Time of Invention)
rubrics_metrics.description: ¶ 8.28: Claim [1] directed to an invention not patentably distinct from claim [2] of commonly assigned [3].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when commonly assigned but no indication they were commonly assigned at the time the invention was made. Also make a 35 U.S.C. 102(e)/103(a) rejection as appropriate. Follow with form paragraph 8.28.01. Explain why claims are not considered distinct in bracket 4 and use additional form paragraphs for obviousness-type double patenting (8.34–8.37).

rubrics_metrics.name: Advisory form paragraph 8.28.01 guidance following 8.28
rubrics_metrics.description: ¶ 8.28.01: Advisory information relating to form paragraph 8.28, explaining that the Office normally will not institute an interference between commonly owned cases and that the assignee can either show common ownership at the time of invention under 35 U.S.C. 103(c) and 37 CFR 1.78(c) or name the prior inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use once in an Office action and only following 8.28. If 103(c)(1) or 103(c)(2) applies, double patenting rejections may obviate or replace certain prior-art rejections; otherwise include appropriate 102/103 rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection form paragraph guidance for 35 U.S.C. 102/103 (7.15, 7.21, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraphs 7.15 (102 rejections), 7.19 (102(f)), 7.21 (103(a)), 7.21.01 (provisional 103(a)), 7.15.01 (provisional 102(e)), 7.15.02 (102(e) with common assignee) provide standard language and examiner notes for rejections under 35 U.S.C. 102 and 103.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow specific examiner notes for prerequisites (e.g., preceding form paragraphs required), include Graham v. Deere test explanation for 103(a) rejections, and use AIPA/pre-AIPA rules for determining 102(e) dates. For applications pending on or after Dec. 10, 2004, do not make or maintain 102(e)/103(a) rejections if the patent is disqualified as prior art under 35 U.S.C. 103(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional rejection practice for copending applications (7.21.01 and 7.15.01)
rubrics_metrics.description: ¶ 7.21.01: Claim provisionally rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103(a) as being obvious over copending application having a common assignee or at least one common inventor. ¶ 7.15.01: Claim provisionally rejected under 35 U.S.C. 102(e) as anticipated by copending application with common assignee or inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These provisional rejections are based on the presumption the copending application will be published or patented. They may be overcome by showings under 37 CFR 1.132 (derivation) or 37 CFR 1.131 (date of invention) or by showing the copending application is disqualified under 35 U.S.C. 103(c). A terminal disclaimer cannot overcome certain provisional 102(e) rejections (see In re Bartfeld). Use appropriate form paragraphs when claims conflict or would be obvious over copending disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminal disclaimer cannot by itself obviate 35 U.S.C. 102 or 103 rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: Rejections under 35 U.S.C. 102 or 35 U.S.C. 103 cannot be obviated solely by the filing of a terminal disclaimer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even when a terminal disclaimer is filed, if the facts support statutory 102 or 103 rejections those rejections must be made or maintained unless disqualified under 35 U.S.C. 103(c) (for certain date ranges).

rubrics_metrics.name: CREATE Act/103(c) disqualification effect on 102(e)/103(a) rejections (Dec. 10, 2004+)
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications pending on or after Dec. 10, 2004, and for reexamination proceedings with certain dates, rejections under 35 U.S.C. 102(e)/103(a) should not be made or maintained if the patent is disqualified under 35 U.S.C. 103(c) as prior art in a 103(a) rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before applying or maintaining 102(e)/103(a) rejections for post-CREATE Act matters, confirm whether the reference is disqualified under 103(c); if disqualified, do not use the reference in a 102(e)/103(a) rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner consideration of provisional rejections when effective filing dates differ
rubrics_metrics.description: If conflicting applications have different effective U.S. filing dates, the examiner should consider making a provisional rejection in the later-filed application based on the earlier application (under 35 U.S.C. 102(e) or 102(e)/103(a)) using form paragraphs 7.15.01 or 7.21.01, and similarly for later-filed application vs. issued patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use provisional rejections to preserve rights when a copending application or patent would become prior art upon publication or patenting; follow form paragraph examiner notes regarding when to give additional double patenting rejections as well.
